title: Chapter 65: Captain Yan
html:
“But I haven’t done anything! Wait there. I’m coming down!” Chen Ge leaned toward the window and peered outside. A large crowd had gathered around the Haunted House, and more people were still arriving.

“Boss, listen to me, surrender while you still can before this gets worse.”

“Surrender, my foot! Just wait for me.” He hung up, threw on his clothes, splashed water over his face, and ran for the door. Then he yanked aside the heavy curtains and dashed through the gates.

The rowdy crowd quieted as soon as Chen Ge appeared. The visitors studied him with curiosity and more than a little disappointment. Clearly, they had expected someone surrounded by police to look less… normal.

Chen Ge had never felt so many eyes on him. He shrank under their attention, but the silence demanded that he say something. “Would someone mind telling me what this is about?”

“You’re Chen Ge?” The officer in charge carried a box under one arm. He was slightly rotund, but sharp, penetrating eyes lent a comical contrast to his baby face.

“Yes.”

“Can I see your identification?”

After a lengthy search, Chen Ge produced his identification card. All the while, he silently studied the officer, whose uniform differed from those worn by Inspector Lee and his men.

“Thank you for your cooperation.” The officer smiled, motioned to the reporters, and opened the box. In an official tone, he announced, “For providing crucial evidence in the Ping An Apartments murder case, the Jiujiang Municipal Bureau of Public Security hereby awards Chen Ge the Level Three Public Security Medal of Honor! May he cherish this honor and continue contributing to the safety and security of our society!”

The formal announcement left Chen Ge bewildered. Everything was happening too quickly for his half-awake mind to follow. As the box was pressed into his hands, he stared at the gleaming medal with a single thought. Where’s the reward money?

The rotund officer drew Chen Ge before the wall of reporters and posed beside him. The ordeal lasted fifteen minutes. Once the crowd dispersed and the reporters left, Chen Ge quietly approached the officer. “Sir, what should I call you?”

“My name is Yan. You can call me Captain Yan. Ol’ Lee from Western Jiujiang and I were classmates. In fact, he’s told me quite a lot about you.” Captain Yan seemed friendly, and his eyes shone with approval. “The way you handled the Ping An Apartments case was impressive. Your instincts and powers of observation while the killer was chasing you surprised both Ol’ Lee and me.”

After such generous praise, Chen Ge was too embarrassed to bring up the reward money. “All I did was run like a madman through the woods. The case never would have been solved without the police. In fact, I’d have been the killer’s latest victim if not for all of you.”

After they exchanged pleasantries, Captain Yan noticed Chen Ge lingering shamelessly beside the police car. Understanding dawned, and he smiled to himself. “Xiao Chen, you’ll have to collect the reward in person from the city bureau. Given the scale of the case, approval took some time, but the money is ready now. I hope you understand.”

“Of course, of course.” Now that he knew where to collect the money, the weight lifted from Chen Ge’s heart.

“I came today to thank you in person. Every unsolved case weighs on an officer’s heart, passed from one generation of police to the next. I worked this case four years ago, so thank you for finally lifting that burden.” Captain Yan smiled sincerely. “By the way, the elderly survivor from Ping An Apartments wants to speak with you. He’s bedridden, has lost the use of his lower body, and can barely talk, but his mind is still sharp. He knows you saved him and solved the mystery of his family’s deaths. He wants to thank you himself.”

“I understand.” To Chen Ge, the case had been a mission assigned by the black phone. To the victims and their family, it meant closure.

“You should visit soon. He’s in the hospital now. Perhaps the excitement was too much, or perhaps the question that kept him alive has finally been answered… Either way, he isn’t doing well.”

After that, Captain Yan got into the car.

“All right, I’ll visit him this afternoon.” Studying the man’s distinctive uniform, Chen Ge sensed that Captain Yan carried far greater responsibilities than he let on. Once the police car departed, park employees crowded around him.

“Boss, are you going to be on television again?!”

“Not bad, there’s even a medal.”

After sending them off, Chen Ge found Uncle Xu in the crowd, and he dragged him to a corner to speak.

“Uncle Xu, what’s the update regarding the rental of the underground parking lot? The money will be coming soon!”

The mention of the underground parking lot made Uncle Xu frown. “This isn’t about the money. Xiao Chen, I can’t stand by and watch you dig your own grave. The park’s attendance keeps falling, and everyone else is trying to get out. Don’t you understand?”

“I understand, and I know what I’m doing,” Chen Ge replied confidently. The Haunted House might hold the key to his parents’ disappearance. Only by expanding it could he gain the means and opportunity to interact with the other world.

“Still as stubborn as ever.” Uncle Xu argued until it became clear that Chen Ge would not budge. At last, he sighed. “Come with me, then. The police brought Mr. Luo to the park too. You might as well speak to him yourself.”

“Director Luo is here?” Chen Ge’s parents had often mentioned the true owner of New Century Park.

“What did you expect? The police cordoned off part of the park. Did you think they wouldn’t notify management? Director Luo has stayed here for the past few days to ensure our full cooperation.” Uncle Xu led Chen Ge to a building on the park’s northern side, its second-tallest structure after the Ferris wheel. “When you meet him, watch what you say. The less you say, the fewer mistakes you’ll make. Understand?”

Chen Ge followed Uncle Xu into the elevator and up to the top floor. They stopped outside an unlocked office. Uncle Xu knocked, and a man in his fifties soon emerged.

The man was of average height, with graying hair and gentle features. His suit bore no designer label, but it was spotless and immaculately pressed.

This is Mr. Luo? He looks nothing like his picture.To Chen Ge, the man looked more like a retired teacher.
